abstract: OrthoDB (https://www.orthodb.org) provides evolutionary and functional annotations of orthologous genes across the broadest range of organismal diversity. It extends experimentally acquired knowledge from well-studied organisms to newly sequenced genomes, delineating orthologous groups (OGs) hierarchically at explicit taxonomic levels and annotating them with collated functional evidence and evolutionary traits. This release updates eukaryotic coverage to 5768 genomes, including 132 mammalian genomes re-annotated with Tiberius, and incorporates an updated selection of the latest available fungal and protist genomes. The OGs were recomputed de novo with OrthoLoger from MMseqs2 candidate homology searches using optimized parameters. To better recover remote homology at the Eukaryota root and among divergent protist sequences, we used the The Embedded Alphabet (TEA) protein-language-model-derived alphabet. This increased OG assignment, with greater representation of least diverged orthologs. BUSCO lineage datasets were rebuilt for eukaryotes using broader and more evenly represented species sampling, further extending their value for metagenome-assembled genomes and microbial eukaryotes. The OrthoDB web interface now includes a source-linked conversational assistant, and a Model Context Protocol layer exposes public API endpoints to external AI agents. OrthoDB remains accessible through the web, bulk downloads, REST, SPARQL/RDF, Python, and R/Bioconductor; BUSCO and OrthoLoger are available from https://busco.ezlab.org and https://orthologer.ezlab.org.
